formulas.name: Velocity
formulas.description: Calculates velocity from displacement over time.

formulas.name: Acceleration
formulas.description: Calculates uniform acceleration from the change in velocity over time.

formulas.name: Force
formulas.description: Relates force, mass, and acceleration.

formulas.name: Force of Gravity
formulas.description: Calculates the force of gravity acting on a mass near the Earth's surface using the textbook value of 9.81 m/s².

formulas.name: Pressure
formulas.description: Calculates pressure from force acting uniformly over an area.

formulas.name: Work
formulas.description: Calculates work when a force moves through a distance in the direction of the force.

formulas.name: Power
formulas.description: Calculates the rate of doing work.

formulas.name: Gravitational Potential Energy
formulas.plainExpression: potential energy = mass × gravity × vertical height
formulas.description: Calculates gravitational potential energy from mass and vertical height.

formulas.name: Kinetic Energy
formulas.description: Calculates the mechanical energy a body has because of motion.

formulas.name: Moment of a Force
formulas.description: Calculates the turning effect of a force about a selected point.

variables.meaning: perpendicular distance from the line of force to the point

formulas.name: Rotational Equilibrium
formulas.description: For a body in rotational equilibrium, clockwise and counterclockwise moments about the same point balance.

formulas.name: Vertical Force Equilibrium
formulas.description: For a body in vertical equilibrium, total upward force equals total downward force.

formulas.name: Actual Mechanical Advantage
formulas.description: Ratio of load to effort for a machine.

formulas.name: Velocity Ratio
formulas.plainExpression: VR = distance moved by effort / distance moved by load
formulas.description: Ratio of effort travel to load travel.

formulas.name: Machine Efficiency
formulas.description: Relates actual mechanical advantage to velocity ratio. Multiply by 100 for percent efficiency.

formulas.name: Wheel and Axle Velocity Ratio
formulas.plainExpression: VR = wheel radius / axle radius = wheel diameter / axle diameter
formulas.description: Velocity ratio for a simple wheel and axle.

formulas.name: Average Speed
formulas.plainExpression: average speed = distance travelled / total time
formulas.description: Average scalar speed over a journey.

formulas.name: Average Velocity
formulas.description: Average vector velocity from displacement over time.

formulas.name: Uniformly Changing Velocity Displacement
formulas.description: Displacement using average velocity when acceleration is uniform.

formulas.name: Uniform Acceleration Velocity
formulas.plainExpression: final velocity = initial velocity + acceleration × time
formulas.description: Relates initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration, and time for constant acceleration.

formulas.name: Uniform Acceleration Without Time
formulas.plainExpression: final velocity² = initial velocity² + 2 × acceleration × displacement
formulas.description: Uniform acceleration relation useful when time is not given.

formulas.name: Uniform Acceleration Displacement
formulas.plainExpression: s = initial velocity × time + 0.5 × acceleration × time²
formulas.description: Displacement under constant acceleration when initial velocity, acceleration, and time are known.

formulas.name: Absolute Pressure
formulas.plainExpression: absolute pressure = gauge pressure + atmospheric pressure
formulas.description: Converts gauge pressure to absolute pressure using atmospheric pressure.

formulas.name: Coefficient of Friction
formulas.plainExpression: coefficient of friction = friction force / normal reaction force
formulas.description: Ratio of friction force to normal reaction force.

formulas.name: Normal Stress
formulas.description: Normal stress intensity from a perpendicular load over cross-sectional area.

formulas.name: Shear Stress
formulas.plainExpression: shear stress = parallel load / shear area
formulas.description: Parallel shear stress intensity from a load over the resisting shear area.

formulas.name: Strain
formulas.plainExpression: strain = change in length / original length
formulas.description: Measures deformation as change in length divided by original length.

formulas.name: Factor of Safety
formulas.plainExpression: factor of safety = ultimate stress / allowable stress
formulas.description: Ratio of ultimate stress to allowable stress.

formulas.name: Power Transmitted by a Belt
formulas.plainExpression: power transmitted = (tight-side tension - slack-side tension) × belt speed
formulas.description: Power transmitted by a belt from the difference in belt tensions and belt speed.

formulas.name: Pulley Speed and Diameter Relationship
formulas.plainExpression: driver speed × driver diameter = driven speed × driven diameter
formulas.description: Ideal belt-drive speed relationship when belt slip is neglected.

formulas.name: Gear Speed Ratio
formulas.plainExpression: driven speed = driver speed × driver teeth / driven teeth
formulas.description: Relates rotational speeds of meshing gears to their tooth counts.

flashcards.front: What is a moment of force?
flashcards.back: The turning effect of a force about a point. Its magnitude is force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the line of force to the point.

flashcards.front: What three balance conditions define equilibrium in Chapter 2?
flashcards.back: Upward forces equal downward forces, rightward forces equal leftward forces, and clockwise moments equal counterclockwise moments.
A single support about which a bar is free to rotate.
Force per unit area, acting normal to a surface.
When a force applied to a body causes it to move through a distance.
The rate of doing work, or work done per unit time.
Resistance that opposes the initial movement of a body at rest.
Resistance that opposes the continued sliding movement of an object.
The ability of a material to return to its original shape after a deforming force is removed.
The ability of a material to retain its deformed shape when a deforming force is removed.
The ability of a material to be stretched and reduced in cross section without breaking.

a-1-c-2.overview: This chapter teaches why balancing only the upward and downward forces is not enough. A beam can have zero net vertical force and still have a turning tendency. Moments account for that turning effect.
keyConcepts: A force creates a moment only when its line of action has a perpendicular distance from the chosen point.
Moment magnitude is force multiplied by perpendicular distance.
Equilibrium requires both force balance and moment balance.
You may take moments about any point, but choosing a support with an unknown reaction usually eliminates that unknown from the moment equation.
Reaction forces at supports are the upward forces that balance the applied loads on a simply supported beam.
remember: Use perpendicular distance, not slant distance.
State the point about which moments are taken.
For equilibrium: clockwise moments equal counterclockwise moments.
After finding one support reaction, use upward forces equal downward forces to find the other.
commonMistakes: Stopping after proving upward force equals downward force. That checks translation, but not rotation.
Using the total beam length as the lever arm for every force instead of each force's distance from the chosen pivot.
Using the slanted distance instead of the perpendicular distance from the force's line of action.
Mixing clockwise and counterclockwise moments without identifying their direction first.

quickCheck.prompt: A 10 N downward force acts 2 m to the right of a pivot. What moment does it create?
If upward forces equal downward forces, is a beam automatically in equilibrium?
quickCheck.answer: No. Clockwise and counterclockwise moments must also balance.

quickCheck.prompt: Why is taking moments about one support useful when solving a simply supported beam?
quickCheck.answer: The reaction at that support has zero perpendicular distance from the pivot, so its moment is zero and it drops out of the equation.
